resources.string: Find lyrics for the whole library
Lyricota finds synced lyrics (word by word when available) and saves them into your songs.
Formats: MP3, FLAC, M4A, OGG, OPUS, WAV…

The best lyrics for each song are found and saved (%1$s), using the current format and romanization.
Lyricota finds synced lyrics from several public sources and saves them into the music files on your device.
Word by word, duets, backing vocals, official romanization and translation. Lyrics through the community service lyrics.paxsenix.org; search through the public iTunes Search API.
Community-made word-by-word lyrics with duets and backing vocals. Lyrics written by contributors are released under CC0 1.0; imported data keeps its original provider\'s terms.
Word by word (QRC) and translations, from the service\'s public web endpoints.

Word by word (YRC) and translations, from the service\'s public web endpoints.
Free API with karaoke and line-synced lyrics.
Open, community-maintained database of line-synced lyrics.

Lyricota does not host, store or redistribute lyrics. It downloads them on demand, only when you ask, and only for your personal use. Lyricota only asks for what it needs. You can change any of these later in Android settings.
To read your songs and write lyrics and tags into them. Only the folder you choose — nothing else on your phone.
To show the progress of batch operations while you use other apps, and to tell you when they finish. Optional.
Lyricota can show this batch\'s progress (%) in a notification and tell you when it finishes, so you can leave the app while it works. Allow notifications?
To search lyrics, metadata and covers. Android grants it when installing; only the title, artist, album and duration of the song being searched are sent.
Synced lyrics and complete metadata for the music on your phone. A quick tour of what it can do:
Tap a song: every source is searched at once and the best result (word by word first) is picked.
Duets (v2) and backing vocals ([bg]) are kept, with romanization for Japanese, Korean and Chinese.
Save it inside the file or as a .lrc next to it. The built-in player lets you check the sync.
Complete title, album, artists, composers, genres, year and track/disc numbers, compared across Deezer, Apple Music and MusicBrainz.
Search for a cover image, one song at a time.
In bulk, changes are applied only when the title and artist match; the rest wait for your approval.
Search the lyrics of any song, even one that isn\'t on your phone, and open a result to preview it.
The button at the top right processes many songs at once: all, the ones missing lyrics or metadata, or the ones you select.
Long-press a song to select several.
A notification shows the percentage while it works and tells you when it reaches 100%.
Lyricota is free, open source and has no ads. If it\'s useful to you, you can buy me a coffee on Ko-fi.

Lyricota has no accounts, ads, analytics or trackers. It only connects to the sources listed above, sending the title, artist, album and duration of the song being searched, and to GitHub to check for new versions (can be turned off in Settings). Your settings and library cache stay on your device.
Reference for the QRC decryption and for the lyrics APIs of QQ Music, Kugou and NetEase. It is the reason Lyricota is licensed under the GPL-3.0.
Android will ask you to confirm. Your settings and library are kept.
When the app opens (at most twice a day) it asks GitHub for the latest version. Nothing about you is sent.
Allow Lyricota to install apps, then come back and tap Install
Like Android, subfolders that contain a .nomedia file (and everything inside them) are not scanned.
Lyrics already saved in this song
The batch didn\'t find a result whose title and artist safely match these songs, so nothing was changed in them.

What to do:
1. Tap a song in the list.
2. If one of the results is right, tap “Use” and then “Accept changes”.
3. If none is right, fix the fields by hand or tap “Reject”: the song stays as it was.
Rejected: %1$d songs stay as they were
No source found this song, so there\'s nothing to apply. You can type the data by hand and tap “Accept changes”, fix the title or artist and search again, or tap “Reject” to leave the song as it is.

resources.string: Copies the lyrics from one place to the other. The original stays, so the song ends up with both.
You can undo it afterwards from ⋮ → Undo last batch.
Names each file with its tags (the .lrc next to it is renamed too).
%1$d songs have title and artist in their tags; %2$d without them are skipped.
“%1$s” from %2$s (%3$d songs) will go back to how the songs were before.
Play the song and tap “Mark” right when each highlighted line starts. Tap a line to select it; long-press to listen from its time. When every line has a time, tap “Done”.
The times you marked will be lost.
Paste the lyrics or open a .lrc / .txt file. If they have no times, you can sync them by hand.
Tap the pencil to fix the title or artist, or paste the lyrics and sync them by hand.
Lyrics added or synced by you
The offset is applied to the lyrics when you save them.
